How a result was made

Source: R/steps.r
ecodive_steps.Rd

ecodive's results record each step that made them in one attribute per step, so that the record travels with the result through later steps:

Details

  • dist: how a distance matrix was computed, set by beta_div(), its metric functions (such as bray()), vlr(), rho_p() and phi_s().

  • ord: how an ordination was computed, set by pcoa(), pca(), dbrda(), procrustes() and every other ordination.

Each record is a small list of class ecodive_step, which str() and print() show on one line. Its first element, name, is the step's display name (such as "Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity" or "Principal Coordinates Analysis"), so that any package can label it without ecodive's tables; the rest are the settings it was made with. Read them as a list: attr(x, "dist")$metric.

The records accumulate as results pass along: an ordination of a distance matrix keeps the matrix's dist record beside its own ord record, and the permutation tests (permanova(), ...) keep their distance matrix's dist, and envfit() its ordination's dist and ord. plot() titles its plots with them, such as "Principal Coordinates Analysis of Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity".

The dist record

  • name: The metric's display name, as list_metrics() gives it.

  • metric: Its ID, such as "bray".

  • norm: The normalization applied before computing it (by name, such as "percent"), whether chosen with norm or fixed by the metric (such as hellinger()'s). Absent for the UniFrac metrics.

  • pseudocount: The pseudocount used (0 for none), for the metrics that take one. denominator, for rho_p() and phi_s().

  • power, alpha: For minkowski() and generalized_unifrac().

  • clust, order: With the clust argument: the clustering method, and each sample's position in the input.

The ord record

  • name: The method's display name, as list_dist_ords() and list_count_ords() give it.

  • method: Its ID, such as "pcoa" (also the ordination's method attribute).

  • The other arguments it was called with that are single values, such as n_axes, correction, seed, norm or formula (as text). Data arguments (dm, counts, data, ...) and cpus, which never changes the result, are left out.

Examples

    ord <- pcoa(bray(iris[, 1:4], norm = 'percent'))
    str(ord)
#>  'ecodive_ord' num [1:150, 1:3] 0.177 0.164 0.174 0.153 0.176 ...
#>  - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
#>   ..$ : NULL
#>   ..$ : chr [1:3] "PCoA1" "PCoA2" "PCoA3"
#>  - attr(*, "method")= chr "pcoa"
#>  - attr(*, "eig")= num [1:3] 2.1337 0.0263 0.0153
#>  - attr(*, "prop")= num [1:3] 0.98139 0.0121 0.00704
#>  - attr(*, "trace")= num 2.17
#>  - attr(*, "correction")= chr "none"
#>  - attr(*, "constant")= num 0
#>  - attr(*, "dist")= Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity (metric = bray, norm = percent, pseudocount = 0)
#>  - attr(*, "ord")= Principal Coordinates Analysis (method = pcoa, n_axes = 3, correction = none)
    attr(ord, 'dist')
#> Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity (metric = bray, norm = percent, pseudocount = 0)
    attr(ord, 'dist')$name
#> [1] "Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity"
    attr(ord, 'ord')$n_axes
#> [1] 3
